issue.body: The response returned by `getResponse` is now the BrowserKit Response (as specified in the phpdoc) instead of the HttpFoundation Response.

body: Unfortunately, I don't think we will be able to fix this as it would break almost all applications using functional testing. The only viable option I can see is to first make the Response class of BrowserKit look more similar to the HttpFoundation class.
@fabpot then you would have to break Goutte, which uses the proper Response. So you need to choose one or the other.

This bit me today.
Any thoughts on fixing?

@fabpot couldn't we do something about it ? Releasing the LTS with a class breaking the contract of its interface looks wrong to me.
And it means that code written for the BrowserKit component cannot be used to test with the HttpKernel Client.

This caught me out yesterday. While ideally there will be a proper fix (does there really need to be two separate classes representing the same thing too?), can @Dattaya's suggestion be used for the moment? (`getRequest()` as well.) This won't break anything, and will stop IDEs (and me!) getting confused.

When using `FrameworkBundle/Test/WebTestCase` and trying to get a `getResponse()` IDEs catching up `BrowserKit\Response` instead of `HttpFoundation\Response`. This causes false-errors and wrong code completion when accessing

``` php
$client = static::createClient();
// ...
$headers = $client->getResponse()->headers
```
- [ ] gather feedback my changes
- [ ] probably there are some annotations magic that can override return class of a method, so nothing will be overloaded

body:
So what's the problem? Need just to extend `Symfony\Component\BrowserKit\Response` from `Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response`. Only one thing i can see after getting this done is I need to store separate `headers` as `array` instead of `ResponseHeaderBag` and rewrite `__toString` and `getHeader` to use `ResponseHeaderBag`. 
BTW. test on Goutte ran okay with changed `Symfony\Component\BrowserKit\Response`. Just need to add `http-fondation` dependency.

As a result of this very problem I suggested a HTTP message PSR (it was also suggested separately as part of a HTTP client proposal a while back, but should really be standalone).

The (still-a-work-in-progress) proposal is at https://github.com/php-fig/fig-standards/pull/72 (see also the [discussion](https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/php-fig/73cM2qq_uho)).

Assuming it comes to fruition and is adopted by the two components it would resolve this (although there's still a BC break).

@stof I see those responses are different, at least by amount of code. What about rewriting `BrowserKit\Response` a bit so it at least will be look like a `HttpFoundation\Response`? At least make `headers` as public property and be an instance`HttpFoundation\ResponseHeaderBag` (but here we'll introduce dependency)? I don't like to have duplicate code, but i can't see other way to have everything fine with `BrowserKit\Response` and make it compatible with `HttpFoundation\Response` so bugs linked here will be solved.

@thewilkybarkid thanks for the thread. It's a good idea to have these things standartized. But if all communities of frameworks that guy mentioned in first thread will not use this code then there are will be just another standard.
